reasoning: The request to delete grasp_end again doesn't change my reasoning from before—after a failed pick the peg could be displaced, so the nearest stored point might not reflect the correct class, and the score is already perfect. I'm inclined to commit nothing substantial, though a minor clarification about grasp_point applying even when a peg is held could be worth adding.

revision.refused: The report asks, for the second round running, to delete grasp_end on both sides and to rewrite rules 1, 3 and 4 of the subgoal instruction so that a retry points at the peg end entry of either class nearest the stored grasp_point. This is the same request refused in round 1, on grounds that still hold: grasp_end is read only when a later step shows nothing held, which is exactly the failed-or-dropped-pick case in which the peg may no longer lie where it lay at start of execution, so the entry nearest the stored coordinate can then be the other end of the peg or an end of another peg. The class the demonstration closed on is a different fact from the stored coordinate and no later step recovers it, so holding it does not duplicate a fact and dropping it would break NECESSITY and leave rule 3 unable to pick the demonstrated end. Committing the deletion now would simply undo the round 1 refusal. The report's remaining suggestions (restating grasp_point's purpose, noting that it is carried even while a peg is held, naming only two fields in the carry-forward sentence) either describe the failure rather than instruct, or follow from the deletion that is not committed; the existing text already says to copy the value unchanged at every later step and to carry all fields forward. Both rounds scored 10/10 on subgoal and memory, so no transition or field value is unsettled. Nothing is committed this round.
